items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I know the fellow who really wrote “Sentimental Journey” was Ben Homer, who was our head arranger for a while.

ctx.x: That’s a good story. Did the bands — needed to have some kind of gimmick at that time, to be competitive with one another?

Yes. Well Les was — it was mainly a hard swing band I thought. And what he tried to do was take some of the classical things, like “March Slave,” “Mexican Hat Dance,” and things like that, which fortunately I had some clarinet solos to play in those. And he did quite well with those. And then he wrote “Sentimental Journey,” which is still going, but I think the fellow who really wrote “Sentimental Journey” was Ben Homer, who was our head arranger for a while. And Les, as all leaders so, put his name on it. I…
And Doris Day sang that, right?
